clue.text: So blustery, shot almost turns around hole

definitions.note: a phrase meaning boastful talk with nothing behind it

indicators.note: shot in the sense of ruined or worn out, so the words that follow are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Something has gone wrong with a golf stroke: a near miss that spins round the cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hole' looks like the target of the shot, but it is part of the fodder: all of ALMOST TURNS AROUND HOLE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone full of bluster and boasting who never delivers, so it fits a blustery person.

clue.text: In an appendage swab picked up lumps

indicators.note: in a down entry, picking something up raises it, so the built letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an gives the article A

indicators.note: the swab is put in, placed within the appendage phrase

parts.note: a tail is an appendage of an animal
a mop is used to swab a deck or floor

explanation.surface: A medical scene: a swab is taken from an appendage and lumps are found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' is not about collecting the swab: in this down entry it turns the whole assembly upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: These are benign fatty tumours, the plural of a medical term for soft swellings under the skin.

clue.text: Manurer's picked another way to work in this?

definitions.text: Manurer's picked another way to work in this?

indicators.note: the letters are worked into another order, so the phrase is a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written: these two letters plus the answer make up the fodder

explanation.surface: A farmer who spreads manure has chosen a different working method.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of MANURERS PICKED are those of the answer plus IN, so 'Manurer's picked' rearranges to the answer with IN; read whole, the clue also describes a manurer's machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm machine that scatters dung over fields is just what someone who manures would choose to work in.

clue.text: Last-minute changes sent out? For edit, this is it

definitions.note: the final syllable of edit is it

indicators.note: the remaining letters change their order, signalling a rearrangement
the letters of the word sent go out of the fodder before the shuffle

explanation.surface: An editor complains that late corrections were dispatched and these are the final word.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S, E, N, T from LASTMINUTE to leave LAMIUT, and rearrange. The definition plays on the term for the last syllable of a word: in 'edit' that is 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means the last syllable of a word, and the final syllable of edit is literally it.

clue.text: Reportedly his best as a climber?

definitions.text: Reportedly his best as a climber?

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word his is taken by its sound

parts.note: said aloud, his matches the plural of hi, a greeting

indicators.note: in a down entry a climber goes upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks

explanation.surface: Someone is said to have done their best work as a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: HIS sounds like HIGHS, plural of the greeting 'hi'; TOP reversed upwards gives POT. A climber's best moment is the summit, which is the whole clue's reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the most enjoyable or memorable moment, literally the highest point a climber reaches.

clue.text: Happy Italian set, obtaining 50 in viva with boost

indicators.note: a boost lifts something up, so in a down entry the letters are read upwards
the set goes inside the viva

parts.note: a viva is an oral examination, so oral

indicators.note: the set word takes in, obtains, the Roman fifty

parts.note: to set is to gel
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An Italian is cheerful after a boost from passing an oral exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With boost' lifts the whole assembly, read bottom to top in this down entry. The answer is Milton's poem, whose Italian title means 'the cheerful man'.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's pastoral poem has an Italian title meaning the cheerful man, so it is literally the happy Italian.

clue.text: e — 11 = HQ

definitions.meaning: first meaning: e is the ... of natural logarithms
second meaning: lacking the quality at 11 across, chivalry, so low and dishonourable
third meaning: headquarters is a military ...

explanation.walkthrough: The symbols make it look like an equation; it is three separate meanings of one word, with 11 standing for the answer at 11 across, a knightly sense of honour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a logarithm root, the ignoble opposite of chivalry, and a military headquarters.

clue.text: See 16
Wheel nut I secure fast!

indicators.note: read as an imperative, wheel means turn round, so the fan is turned back to front

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast, a fan
to lash is to tie securely

explanation.surface: A mechanic tightens a wheel nut quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wheel nut' is a car part in the surface, but 'Wheel' is a command to turn the next word back.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means instantly or very quickly, as if in a burst of light.

clue.text: Accentuate every second to help pitch and keep piece impressive

indicators.note: stress each second letter, so only the alternate letters are taken

explanation.surface: Advice to a musician: stress each second beat to keep the pitch and the piece impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking every second letter of HELP PITCH gives the answer, and so does every second letter of KEEP PIECE: the clue gives the same word twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: On a grand, heroic scale, as a sweeping film or poem is, so very impressive.

clue.text: Routes sleeper may take in king's honour

indicators.note: the routes go inside the king's letters

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king, and S marks the possessive
a sleeper train runs on night lines

explanation.surface: A railway story: an overnight train route named in honour of a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleeper' looks like someone in bed but is an overnight train, whose routes are night lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means chivalry, the conduct expected of a knight, which is a sense of honour.

clue.text: From underneath seat, shy sister has caught part of service

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from underneath means from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to seat someone is to sit them
shy means timid

explanation.surface: A timid nun is caught sitting on something odd in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From underneath' turns only the last two words, read bottom to top in this down entry. The answer is the Song of Simeon, sung at Evensong.
explanation.definitionFit: The Song of Simeon is a canticle sung during Evensong and Compline, so it forms one part of the liturgy.

clue.text: Hawk perhaps besieging a twisting road?

parts.note: a warp is a twist, as in a warped plank
a lane is a narrow road

explanation.surface: A bird of prey circling over a winding country road.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hawk is a British jet aircraft, not the bird. 'Besieging' only adds the military flavour to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hawk is a British military jet, so it is an example of a combat aircraft.

clue.text: See 16
10 Ben's known for filming and his part therein

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the words just given, lying in them

explanation.surface: Ben Kingsley is famous for filming an epic and the role he played in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is the answer at 10 across, EPIC: Ben Kingsley won an Oscar for the title role in Attenborough's 1982 biopic.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Kingsley's best-known film, an Oscar-winning biopic of the Indian independence leader, is the epic he is known for.

clue.text: Substitute tackles awfully deep player

indicators.note: to tackle something is to take it on, so the substitute word holds the other letters

parts.note: tack, to change course, taken as to substitute one direction for another

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters of deep are jumbled

explanation.surface: A football substitute makes a dreadful tackle on a deep-lying player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Substitute' and 'player' both look like football; the player is an audio machine for cassettes, and the substitute word stretches the sense of changing tack.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that plays and records cassette tapes is an audio player.

clue.text: Misunderstanding Doc's week — then fortnight — off?

indicators.note: off means wrong or gone bad, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient is confused about whether the doctor signed them off for one week or two.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a sick note, but all of DOCS WEEK THEN FORTNIGHT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for misinterpreting a situation is to grasp a stick by its incorrect end, so it means a misunderstanding.

clue.text: See 1
Constituents you need to create a setter's protein

indicators.note: the answer is read as a list of building blocks, the pieces that together make up the next two words

parts.note: a setter writing a setter's means a mine, with mine split into two parts

explanation.surface: A recipe: the ingredients needed to make a crossword setter's favourite protein.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as 'A, M AND INE': those are the constituents that make A MINE, which is what a setter says for 'a setter's'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a globulin found in almonds and other nuts, a plant protein.

clue.text: See 16
Driver imbibing not one? Yes and no!

definitions.text: Driver imbibing not one? Yes and no!

indicators.note: to imbibe is to take in, so the driver holds the zero

parts.note: a car user is someone who drives
not one is nought, the letter that looks like zero

explanation.surface: A quizzical aside about whether a driver drinks or abstains.
explanation.walkthrough: A drinker who goes driving is both imbibing and not, hence 'Yes and no!'; the whole clue doubles as the definition of a hard drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A reveller who drinks heavily takes in drink, so it describes a drinker who might also drive.

clue.text: Portico without opening agitated god of the sun

indicators.note: lose the opening, so the first letter of the word goes

parts.note: vexed means agitated
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A sun god is angered by a porch with no way in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without opening' sounds like a description of the portico, but it removes the first letter of VEXED.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical architecture this is a recess or open colonnade with seats, akin to a portico.

clue.text: This is a surprise filling in small fish pudding

indicators.note: the exclamation fills, goes inside, the fish

parts.note: fry are young, small fish
lumme is a British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A surprise: a small fish turns up inside a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: LUMME (also lummy) is an old British cry of astonishment, like 'Lord love me'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a soft sweet dish set with oatmeal or gelatine, a kind of dessert.

clue.text: Dicky, heading off out, does — and did

indicators.note: dicky means shaky or unsound, so the letters are rearranged
the heading, the first letter, is taken off the word out

explanation.surface: Someone called Dicky goes out and carries on as before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name but is the anagram signal for UT plus DOES.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'I used to go there', the phrase expresses a past habit, the same as did in that sense.

clue.text: Out again on vintage line

parts.note: re means on, concerning
a cru is a vineyard or its wine, a vintage
descent is a line of ancestry

explanation.surface: A wine merchant brings a vintage range back on sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out again' means breaking out once more, as a disease does, not back on the shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a disease or trouble recurring after a dormant period, breaking forth once more.

clue.text: Talk of pi folk, thin on the ground but thinner on top

definitions.note: pi means pious, so this is sanctimonious talk

indicators.note: like a balding head, the word loses its top letter in this down entry

parts.note: scant means scarce, thin on the ground

explanation.surface: Pious people are scarce, and balding too.
explanation.walkthrough: Pi is slang for pious; 'thinner on top' takes the first letter off SCANT in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means hypocritical sanctimonious talk, the language associated with pious people.

clue.text: See 5
Chum for mum

parts.note: to can mean for, as on a gift label: to Mum
mum means silent, and sh is a call for silence

explanation.walkthrough: 'For mum' reads like a gift tag; in fact it is TO and SH. The answer is a British form of address to a man, like mate.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a casual British way of addressing a man, used like mate or pal.

clue.text: Console producer, not having secured design

indicators.note: the word for not holds, has secured, the design

parts.note: no means not, as in no good
to intend is to design, as in designed for

explanation.surface: A games console maker refuses a design it has acquired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Console' is a games console, not comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese company makes games consoles such as the Switch, so it is a console manufacturer.
